paths.description: Homepage and primary game-discovery entry; covers global navigation, consent, preferences, accessibility, performance, security and discovery.
Action category listing representing category/index templates and dense game-tile navigation.
Subway Surfers detail and embedded runtime representing the core browse-to-play journey, rich media, game startup and memory footprint.
Deliberately invalid route used to verify HTTP and user-facing recovery state.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt its bright palette to the user’s dark-mode preference.
findings.evidence: With prefers-color-scheme: dark emulated, the body remains rgb(131, 255, 231), and DOM/CSS inspection found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface and text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Continuous homepage animation remains active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports two running animations with 6000ms duration under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; CSS inspection found no reduced-motion query.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that stops continuous decorative motion and removes non-essential transitions.

findings.summary: The consent UI does not provide sufficient contrast in a critical preference/control surface.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured a 2.91:1 ratio for the blue consent link and all three blue/white consent buttons, below the required 4.5:1 for their text size.
findings.suggestedFix: Use contrast-safe consent colors and verify them in forced-colors and prefers-contrast modes; avoid overriding system colors where they improve visibility.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the complete game catalogue on every clean first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a modal-like consent panel plus blurred backdrop covering the primary content before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface where legally possible, preserve equally prominent choices, and avoid blocking browsing before optional processing begins.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is custom notification-stack markup rather than a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no dialog, role=dialog, or popover for the full-screen consent experience; the Lighthouse DOM path identifies nested div/button custom chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal consent with <dialog> and correct focus management, or a non-modal semantic region if the content need not be blocked.

findings.summary: The consent surface breaks narrow-screen reflow.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, the layout primitive reports scrollWidth/innerWidth 644px versus a 360px visual viewport, producing 284px horizontal overflow; the screenshot clips copy and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the dialog minimum width, constrain it with max-inline-size: calc(100vi - 2rem), use logical padding, and stack actions at narrow container sizes.

findings.summary: Reusable grid, navigation and consent components rely on viewport styles rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: Across the homepage, category and game DOM/CSS captures, no @container rule was found; the consent component consequently overflows its narrow containing viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable components containment and use @container rules for action stacking and tile/grid changes, retaining viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance misses the Core Web Vitals loading bar, especially on the main landing experience.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.9s, CLS 0.149 and performance 66 on the homepage; the game trace independently measured LCP 4.16s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP asset, reduce critical dependency depth, reserve all late UI space, and defer game/runtime work until it is needed.

findings.summary: The homepage shifts visibly during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.149 and failed its layout-shift-culprits insight; the independent mobile layout observer also saw a shift of 0.068 before dismissal.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for notification and image regions, stabilize font fallbacks, and avoid inserting consent chrome after the initial layout.

findings.summary: The representative game route blocks the main thread during startup.
findings.evidence: The game trace recorded 8 long tasks, a 338.91ms longest task and 827.28ms total blocking time over an 11.4s trace.
findings.suggestedFix: Split game startup into prioritized chunks, yield between initialization phases, and move suitable parsing/asset work off the main thread.

findings.summary: The loading dependency surface is broad and delays readiness.
findings.evidence: The homepage requests 17 stylesheets and 81 scripts; the game route requests 427 resources including 134 scripts. HAR summaries identify 10 parser-inserted very-high-priority stylesheets on each template.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer route-specific styles and scripts, and audit priority hints so only resources needed for the current viewport compete early.

findings.summary: Several controls and game images expose inconsistent or missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three label/content-name mismatches (Search, company page, language), while the game image audit found two images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each visible label part of its accessible name, label the search input directly, and use meaningful alt text or empty alt for decorative game backgrounds.

findings.summary: Consent links and actions fail WCAG text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.91:1 for “here”, “More Options”, “Accept” and “Reject” in the consent panel, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the action blue or adjust foreground/background tokens to at least 4.5:1, then retest all consent states.

findings.summary: The homepage emits an avoidable console/network error on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a failed 401 request to https://poki-auth.poki.com/sessions/whoami as a browser console error.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat unauthenticated state as an expected response without a failing request, or avoid calling whoami until authentication state requires it.

findings.summary: The game template includes unsized and inaccessible image assets.
findings.evidence: The game image audit found 15 images without width/height, including 960px game backgrounds, plus 7 oversized images; this weakens asset structure and shift prevention.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio to all content and background image elements and retain CDN responsive transforms.

findings.summary: The main document cannot use the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons, led by Cache-Control: no-store on the main resource and a no-store JavaScript request.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove no-store from public catalogue documents where safe and isolate truly sensitive responses so back navigation can restore instantly.

findings.summary: The consent privacy link uses non-descriptive link text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO reports one link whose entire text is “here”, pointing to /en/privacy.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace “here” with a self-contained label such as “Read Poki’s cookie and privacy details”.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, nosniff and frame-ancestors, but Permissions-Policy is absent; the CSP only declares frame-ancestors and provides no script/style/object restriction.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP beyond frame-ancestors and add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy for sensors, camera, microphone and other capabilities.

findings.summary: The manifest advertises an app-like experience without a registered service worker or offline cache.
findings.evidence: The manifest has a start_url and app icons, but the live PWA probe found zero service-worker registrations and zero Cache Storage entries.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker with a small offline shell/fallback and cache only proportionate catalogue assets; verify flaky-network recovery.

findings.summary: The game route eagerly transfers a large runtime before the user starts playing.
findings.evidence: The game HAR recorded 427 requests and 9.73MB transferred in seven seconds, including 8.05MB of fetch/XHR and a 1.95MB environment bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate full game bundles behind explicit play intent, load an idle/minimal bundle first, and stage audio, characters and environment assets by gameplay need.
